items.a: AVRIX is a cyber security provider for UK and European businesses. We offer penetration testing, 24/7 managed security monitoring, compliance support (Cyber Essentials, ISO 27001, SOC 2, UK GDPR, EU GDPR, PCI DSS, NIS2 and DORA), incident response and security products, all from one team.

Small and medium-sized businesses through to larger organisations across the UK and Europe, in sectors including financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, retail, technology, the public sector and education.
Every engagement is delivered by AVRIX with our specialist team. You have one contract, one point of contact and one team accountable for the results.

items.q: How quickly can you start a security assessment or penetration test?
items.a: We normally hold a free scoping call within a few working days of your enquiry. Once the scope and written authorisation are agreed, testing can usually be scheduled quickly, with urgent work prioritised.

items.q: Will testing disrupt our live systems?
items.a: Testing is planned to avoid disruption. We agree testing windows, limit traffic and avoid destructive techniques unless you approve them. Sensitive systems can be tested out of hours or in a staging environment.

items.q: Do you retest after we fix the issues?
items.a: Yes. Penetration tests include a retest of the reported issues once you've fixed them, with an updated report you can share with customers and auditors.

Yes, when it's authorised. Testing systems without the owner's permission is an offence under the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990, and similar laws apply across Europe. We never start without a signed scope and written authorisation.

items.q: Which standard should we start with?
items.a: For UK businesses, Cyber Essentials is usually the first step and is required for many public sector contracts. ISO 27001 is the most recognised standard across the UK and Europe, and SOC 2 is what US customers usually ask for. We'll recommend the right route based on your customers and regulators.

items.q: Do NIS2 and DORA apply to UK businesses?
items.a: They're EU laws, so they don't apply in the UK directly. But UK businesses providing in-scope services in the EU may be covered, and many EU customers now write NIS2 or DORA requirements into supplier contracts. The UK has its own NIS Regulations, which are being strengthened.

No. Certificates and audit reports are issued by independent, accredited bodies, such as IASME-licensed bodies for Cyber Essentials and UKAS-accredited bodies for ISO 27001. We prepare you and support you through the audit.

items.q: Is 24/7 monitoring only for large companies?
items.a: No. Smaller businesses are frequent targets because they rarely have anyone watching. We size managed detection and SOC services to the number of users and systems you have.
We agree data locations during onboarding. For UK and EU clients, monitoring data can be kept in UK or EU regions to support UK GDPR and EU GDPR requirements.

items.q: We think we've been hacked. What should we do?
items.a: Disconnect affected devices from the network but leave them switched on. Don't delete anything, don't pay a ransom and don't contact the attacker. Then contact us straight away and mark your enquiry as urgent. If personal data may be affected, you may need to report it to the ICO or relevant EU authority within 72 hours.

items.q: Can you help us prepare before an incident?
items.a: Yes. We write incident response plans and ransomware playbooks, test your backups and run tabletop exercises so your team knows what to do.

Testing and compliance projects are quoted at a fixed price after a free scoping call. Managed services are a monthly fee based on the number of users and systems. Incident response can be arranged on demand or through a retainer.
Yes. We're happy to sign a mutual confidentiality agreement before you share anything sensitive.

items.q: How do you handle our data during an engagement?
items.a: We only access what the agreed scope requires, use test accounts wherever possible, store findings securely and delete engagement data when it's no longer needed, in line with our contract and data protection law.
